user.title: Load Insights
user.description:
Reads what your Energy dashboard already knows and forecasts consumption from it. Nothing is re-entered here.

Found in the Energy dashboard: {grid} grid, {solar} PV, {battery} battery, {devices} individual devices, {forecasts} PV forecast entries.

data_description.name: Shown as the device that groups the forecast sensors.
data_description.weather_entity: Supplies the coming week's temperatures. Pre-filled when the instance has exactly one weather entity.
data_description.outdoor_temperature_entity: Supplies the past weeks' temperatures from its statistics. Together with the weather entity it lets the forecast respond to cold and hot spells; a sensor whose temperature turns out not to matter for consumption is ignored automatically.
data_description.calendar_entities: Link any calendars. Load Insights works out from past events what each one means for consumption - an away calendar, a bookings calendar - and ignores one that turns out to mean nothing. Event titles are learned separately where they differ from the calendar's average.
data_description.input_entities: Any entity worth trying as an explanation - a tariff block, an electricity price, irradiance, an occupancy sensor. Load Insights works out from its recorded history whether it explains consumption, and ignores it if not. A sensor with few values is used as it is; a numeric one is cut into bands.

abort.no_energy_dashboard: The Energy dashboard has no grid source configured. Set up at least the grid there first; PV, battery and individual devices improve the forecast.
abort.already_configured: Load Insights is already set up.

inputs.title: Explanatory inputs
inputs.description: Inputs the forecast may learn from. Each is kept only if it actually explains consumption.

device_state.title: Device state sensor
device_state.description: Pick a device from the Energy dashboard and the sensor that says what it is about to do - a boiler's tank temperature, a pump's tank level. Its recent value then sharpens that device's forecast for the next six hours. One device per visit; leave the sensor empty to clear it.

detection.title: Load detection

data_description.device: Pick the meter and its per-phase readings are filled in below for you to check. Leave it empty to choose the entities by hand. Submitting the same meter again fills in any field still empty, and never changes one you set yourself.

naming.title: Name a detected load
naming.description:
Loads no device meter accounts for, biggest first - {count} of them, {hidden} more than fit here. Click one to see it and give it a name; naming brings you back to this list.

Each row is: power (phases), energy per week and per run, how long a run lasts, what it might be, and its week from Monday to Sunday. Give two the SAME name to say they are one device on different settings. Choose *finished* when you are done - that is what rebuilds the entities.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description:
What Load Insights sees right now.

{overview}

reset_detection.title: Reset load detection?
reset_detection.description: The signature library and every name in it are forgotten, and the last ten days of the meter are read again from scratch. It runs on its own and takes a while. Do this after a change to the meter, a rewired phase, or an update that changes how loads are found.

grid.title: Grid connection

data_description.grid_device: Pick it and the per-phase readings are filled in below. Leave empty to choose by hand.
data_description.layout: Leave this on automatic and it is read off the data: a grid reading that moves against the inverter's is in parallel with it. Override it where the data cannot say, such as a site that never exports.
data_description.source_kind: The same AC input can be the utility or a generator, and the wiring cannot tell them apart. It decides what a shortfall means: energy bought, a generator someone has to start, or a load that goes unserved.

naming_detail.title: Name this load
naming_detail.description:
{detail}

Type a name to give it entities of its own. Leaving the box empty changes nothing and takes you back to the list, which is as close to a back button as a form allows.

abort.no_devices: The Energy dashboard lists no individual devices.
abort.no_detection: Load detection is not set up: choose the main meter first.
abort.nothing_to_name: Nothing to name yet - either no loads have been detected, or every one is already accounted for by a device meter.

temperature_pair_incomplete.title: The weather response needs both halves
temperature_pair_incomplete.description: Load Insights has the {have} but not the {missing}. The temperature response is fitted on the sensor's recorded past and applied to the weather entity's coming week, so one without the other can never take effect. Add the missing one under Configure -> Explanatory inputs, or clear both.

no_pv_forecast.title: No PV forecast is linked to the Energy dashboard
no_pv_forecast.description: This site produces PV, but its Energy dashboard has no forecast integration linked to the solar source. The grid forecast therefore predicts a week of sunless days, and its import figures are badly pessimistic. Link one (Solcast, Forecast.Solar and others) to the PV source in Settings -> Dashboards -> Energy.

battery_not_modelled.title: The battery is not being modelled
battery_not_modelled.description: The Energy dashboard has a battery at this site, but not {missing}. Without it the state of charge cannot be forecast, so no SOC forecast sensor is created and the grid forecast is the net BEFORE the battery - it says so in its battery_modelled attribute. Both are optional fields on the battery source in Settings -> Dashboards -> Energy.

no_power_factor.title: Some phases cannot tell a heater from a motor
no_power_factor.description: Load detection has a power reading on phase {phases} but no way to work out a power factor there: that needs the phase's current AND voltage, or a power factor sensor. Watts alone cannot separate a 2 kW heater from a 2 kW motor, so detected loads on those phases get no guess at what they are. Add them under Configure -> Load detection.

detection_found_nothing.title: Load detection has found nothing at all
detection_found_nothing.description: The whole history has been read - {samples} readings - and not one load was found. A meter that never moves is the usual cause: an inverter's AC INPUT reads zero at an off-grid site, for instance, while the loads are all on its output. Point load detection at the reading that carries what the house actually draws, under Configure -> Load detection. Devices with their own meters are unaffected.

devices_without_power.title: Some metered devices cannot be detected
devices_without_power.description: {devices} appear on the Energy dashboard but publish no power reading, only energy. Hourly energy is far too coarse to line up with a load switching on, so these devices cannot locate or name anything in load detection. Their forecasts are unaffected.

options.auto: Work it out from the data
options.parallel: Parallel - inverter feeds the grid bus directly (AC-coupled solar, no battery)
options.series: Series - all power flows through the inverter (hybrid with DC-coupled battery)
